ambition.goal_beyond: Guests who leave happy and say so, so the rating and bookings hold without the restaurant having to chase them

research.approach: Practitioners treat a rating drop as a symptom of something that changed in service, and start from the raw review text and dates, not the star average. They tag every low review by theme, date it against the staffing and menu changes, and check whether the booking fall follows the rating or has other causes such as availability, seasons or the booking path. Fixes go to the cause with the head chef (peak-night capacity, pass checks for hot food, menu items that cannot be plated fast), while the front of house replies to reviews in a plain, specific way and invites every guest to review without rewards, because Google penalises incentives and selective asking. Because a lifetime average moves slowly, they read the rating of recent reviews separately and work out how many good reviews the target needs before promising a date.

steps.name: Load every review with date, stars and text, and tag each low review by theme
steps.why: The 18 one- and two-star reviews are the raw evidence; dated themes show what guests mean and when it began.

steps.name: Line up complaint dates with the kitchen change, menu change and booking numbers
steps.why: Cause shows in timing: complaints that start with a change point to that change.

steps.name: Check the booking drop by channel and the booking path
steps.why: Bookings can fall because of availability, the booking link, season or the rating, and each has a different fix.

steps.name: Separate unfair or off-topic reviews from fair ones
steps.why: Only reviews that break Google's policies can be removed; the rest need an answer, not a report.

steps.name: Find the service and kitchen cause with the head chef and fix it
steps.why: Slow service and cold food are operating problems, and replies cannot fix them.

steps.name: Reply to reviews specifically and invite every guest to review without rewards
steps.why: Replies show guests and future guests the response, and an honest invitation rebuilds the rating within Google's rules.

steps.name: Work out how many good reviews 4.4 needs and read recent reviews separately
steps.why: A lifetime average moves slowly, so the date promised must match the review flow.

steps.name: Read the rating, review themes and bookings weekly
steps.why: Weekly reading shows whether the fix is working before the average moves.

steps.name: Offer guests a discount or free item for leaving a review
steps.why: A common way to speed up review volume.

pitfalls.text: Replying to reviews and asking for more while the cause (slow service, cold food) goes on, so new low reviews keep arriving.
Asking only happy guests for reviews or offering anything in return, which Google treats as a violation and the owner has ruled out.
Reporting fair but harsh reviews as fake; only policy-breaking reviews can be removed.
Blaming the new menu or the new kitchen team without dating the complaints against each change.
Promising a rating date without working out how many good reviews the average needs.
Reading the booking drop as a rating effect when availability, the booking link or the season also changed.

hypotheses.statement: The complaints started after the August kitchen team change.
hypotheses.test: Count one- and two-star reviews per week, before and after the change date, with the themes.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 80% of the complaint reviews are dated after the change and weekly low reviews at least doubled.
hypotheses.refute_if: Low reviews were already rising before the change.

hypotheses.statement: Slow service happens on peak nights or when bookings per slot are high.
hypotheses.test: Match complaint review dates and any ticket times to covers per slot and weekday.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than half of the complaints fall on the busiest 2 nights or slots, or order-to-table time rises with covers.
hypotheses.refute_if: Complaints are spread evenly across nights and covers.

hypotheses.statement: Cold food comes from the pass, runners or dish design, not from the whole kitchen.
hypotheses.test: Which dishes and which sections of the room the cold-food reviews name; time from pass to table if logged.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Cold-food reviews name a small set of dishes or tables, or logged pass-to-table time is over the set limit.
hypotheses.refute_if: Cold-food reviews name many unrelated dishes and tables and logged times are within the limit.

hypotheses.statement: The new menu is part of the problem.
hypotheses.test: Share of complaint reviews that name a dish added or changed since the menu change, and plating time of those dishes.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 30% of complaint reviews name new or changed dishes.
hypotheses.refute_if: Complaints name old and new dishes alike, or none by name.

hypotheses.statement: Floor or kitchen staffing did not match covers on the nights people complained.
hypotheses.test: Covers per floor and kitchen staff on complaint nights against nights without complaints.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Covers per staff member are higher on complaint nights by 20% or more.

hypotheses.statement: Bookings fell because of the rating, not because of availability, season or the booking path.
hypotheses.test: Bookings by channel before and after, seats offered, the date the fall began against the date the rating fell, and the same weeks last year.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Channels that show the rating fell at least 1.5 times as much as phone and own-site bookings, and the fall began after the rating fell.
hypotheses.refute_if: All channels fell alike, seats offered fell, the fall began before the rating, or last year shows the same dip.

hypotheses.statement: Low reviews have gone unanswered, which leaves the complaints unanswered for future guests.
hypotheses.test: Share of one- and two-star reviews with a reply in the last 3 months.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Fewer than half have a reply.

hypotheses.statement: A rating of 4.4 within three months is reachable only if the flow of good reviews is high enough.
hypotheses.test: New 5-star reviews needed to lift the average to 4.4 from the review count and total, against the weekly review rate now.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The needed number is more than what 12 weeks of reviews at the present weekly rate would bring.
hypotheses.refute_if: The present rate delivers the needed number in 12 weeks or less.

dropped.reason: The owner said never to offer anything in exchange for reviews, and Google treats rewards for reviews as a violation.

measurement.window: Weekly for 12 weeks from the first change, comparing the weeks since the fix with the 8 weeks before, and the same weeks last year if available.
measurement.min_volume: At least 30 new reviews since the fix before the rating is called a result, and at least 4 weeks of bookings per period compared.
measurement.stop_rule: Roll back a kitchen or service change that makes order-to-table time worse for two weeks in a row; stop any reply or invitation that anyone reports as pressure or reward.
